sources: NPS Santa Rosa Island Hiking Guide
NPS Santa Cruz Island Hiking Guide

trails.bestSeason: Year-round; Dec-Mar is best for gray whale sightings from the bluffs
trails.trailTip: Stay on the established path along the bluff edge — the cliffs are undercut in places — and bring binoculars to scan for migrating gray whales offshore instead of leaning out over the rim.
trails.didYouKnow: Cavern Point Loop is the most-hiked trail in the park because it starts right at the Scorpion Anchorage pier where the Island Packers ferry lands.

trails.bestSeason: Year-round; calmest boat landings are typically Apr-Oct
trails.trailTip: This East Anacapa trail follows a flat marine terrace after an initial staircase climb from the landing cove — watch for nesting western gulls right beside the path in early summer and go around them rather than crowding in for a photo.
trails.didYouKnow: Reaching any trail on Anacapa Island means climbing a steep 157-step staircase from the boat landing cove — it's the only way onto the island.

trails.trailTip: Follow the marked bluff-top path from the Cavern Point junction and keep back from the crumbling cliff edge above the cove — the drop is sheer and unfenced.
trails.didYouKnow: The horseshoe-shaped cove was named for its resemblance, seen from above, to a hollowed-out potato.

trails.bestSeason: Year-round; can be muddy after winter rain
trails.trailTip: The descent to Prisoners Harbor loses elevation gradually through island scrub — carry more water than you think you'll need, since there's no shade or water source along the way.
trails.didYouKnow: Prisoners Harbor was a working ranch and shipping point for Santa Cruz Island long before the island became parkland.

trails.bestSeason: Year-round; check current conditions before visiting — as of September 2026, per NPS.gov, Santa Rosa Island reopened for day use on July 1, 2026 after a wildfire burned roughly 18,000 acres (about 40% of the island) in May-June 2026, and some backcountry areas in the island's southeastern quadrant remain closed for the rest of the 2026 season.
trails.trailTip: As of September 2026, per NPS.gov, confirm Santa Rosa Island's current access status before you go — post-fire recovery work is ongoing and some areas are still closed.
trails.didYouKnow: Water Canyon Beach is one of the longest stretches of undeveloped white-sand beach in Southern California.

trails.bestSeason: Year-round; check current conditions before visiting — as of September 2026, per NPS.gov, Santa Rosa Island reopened for day use on July 1, 2026 after a May-June 2026 wildfire, with some backcountry areas still closed for the remainder of the 2026 season.
trails.trailTip: As of September 2026, per NPS.gov, check Santa Rosa Island's current conditions page before planning this hike, since post-fire closures are still in effect in parts of the island.
trails.didYouKnow: This grove is one of only two natural populations of Torrey pine on Earth — the other is near San Diego, over 175 miles away.

trails.bestSeason: Year-round; check current conditions before visiting — as of September 2026, per NPS.gov, Santa Rosa Island reopened for day use on July 1, 2026 after a May-June 2026 wildfire, with some backcountry areas still closed for the remainder of the 2026 season.
trails.trailTip: As of September 2026, per NPS.gov, confirm current access before setting out — this route crosses backcountry terrain on Santa Rosa Island that may still be affected by the 2026 fire closures.
trails.didYouKnow: Lobo Canyon's colorful, wind-carved sandstone walls are one of the most photographed features on Santa Rosa Island.

trails.bestSeason: Fall-Spring; avoid summer heat with no shade or water sources
trails.trailTip: Carry all the water you'll need for the full day — there are no reliable water sources along the route to the island's highest point.
trails.didYouKnow: At 2,450 feet, Signal Peak is the highest point in Channel Islands National Park.

animals.whereToLook: Near campgrounds, trailheads, and open scrub on Santa Cruz and Santa Rosa Islands
animals.viewingTip: If one crosses your path, stay still and watch quietly from a distance with binoculars — never offer food, since foxes that learn to approach hikers for scraps lose their natural wariness and are far more likely to be struck by vehicles.
animals.didYouKnow: The island fox was on the brink of extinction in the late 1990s and, after a captive-breeding and reintroduction program, became the fastest mammal recovery in Endangered Species Act history — it was delisted in 2016.

animals.bestSeason: Pupping and breeding season runs roughly May-Jul at some haul-outs
animals.whereToLook: Rocky ledges and coves around Anacapa and San Miguel Islands
animals.viewingTip: View hauled-out sea lions from at least 50 feet away using binoculars or a zoom lens — approaching closer can startle a mother into abandoning a pup on the rocks.
animals.didYouKnow: San Miguel Island hosts one of the largest and most diverse pinniped haul-outs in the world, with several seal and sea lion species breeding side by side.

animals.whereToLook: Oak and pine woodlands around Scorpion Ranch and the Santa Cruz Island interior
animals.viewingTip: Scan the oak canopy and listen for its harsh, scolding call — a pair of binoculars will show off its noticeably larger size and deeper blue color compared to mainland scrub-jays without needing to approach the trees they're feeding in.
animals.didYouKnow: The Island Scrub-Jay lives only on Santa Cruz Island, making it the only bird species in the U.S. restricted to a single island.

animals.bestSeason: Dec-Mar southbound migration; Mar-May northbound migration
animals.whereToLook: Open water visible from Cavern Point, Potato Harbor, and other bluff-top overlooks
animals.viewingTip: Scan the horizon with binoculars for a blow or fluke — whales are viewed from shore or a boat at a legal distance and should never be approached by watercraft.
animals.didYouKnow: Gray whales migrate roughly 10,000-12,000 miles round trip between Arctic feeding grounds and Baja California breeding lagoons, passing directly by the islands.

animals.bestTimeOfDay: Midday, when light penetrates the kelp forest
animals.whereToLook: Kelp forests and rocky reefs around Anacapa and Santa Cruz Islands
animals.viewingTip: Snorkel or dive slowly and let the fish approach on its own — garibaldi are naturally curious and territorial, so there's no need to chase or corner one for a closer look.
animals.didYouKnow: The garibaldi is California's official state marine fish, and it's illegal to take or harass one anywhere in California waters.

animals.whereToLook: Rocky beaches and tidal ledges throughout the islands
animals.viewingTip: Watch from a bluff or boat with binoculars and keep well back from haul-out sites, especially in spring — a mother that's disturbed may abandon a pup left resting alone on the rocks.
animals.didYouKnow: Harbor seal pups can swim within hours of birth but spend much of their first weeks hauled out resting beside their mothers.

animals.whereToLook: Sea cliffs on Anacapa Island's West End, and shorelines throughout the park
animals.viewingTip: Watch nesting cliffs from a boat or a designated overlook with binoculars and keep well back from the nest ledges — pelicans that flush from a nest can expose eggs or chicks to gulls and sun.
animals.didYouKnow: Anacapa Island hosts the largest breeding colony of California Brown Pelicans in the western United States, a major recovery story after the species nearly vanished here due to DDT pollution.

animals.bestTimeOfDay: Look under natural cover during the day; they are secretive rather than truly nocturnal
animals.bestSeason: Year-round; most active in warmer months
animals.whereToLook: Under driftwood, rocks, and dense vegetation on San Clemente, Santa Barbara, and San Nicolas Islands
animals.viewingTip: If you flip a log or rock to look, set it back exactly as you found it afterward — this species shelters under the same surface debris for cover from predators and drying out.
animals.didYouKnow: The Island Night Lizard gives birth to live young instead of laying eggs, an adaptation shared by several other Channel Islands reptiles.
